title: Tokenized Finance (IMF Note 2026/001, by Tobias Adrian)
key_claim: IMF frames tokenization as 'fundamental reconfiguration of financial architecture': atomic settlement, continuous liquidity management, embedded compliance, with stablecoins as bridge asset but exposed to redemption-run risk; recommends clearer legal frameworks and global coordination.
notes: IMF Tier 1 institutional note authored by Tobias Adrian, head of MCM.

title: CFTC FAQ on Tokenized Collateral and Crypto Asset Use by Registrants
key_claim: CFTC's MPD and DCR jointly issued 11 FAQs (20 March 2026) addressing how FCMs, DCOs and swap dealers may use crypto assets and blockchain under existing CFTC regulations and Staff Letters 25-39 (tokenized collateral guidance) and 26-05 (no-action position permitting payment stablecoins, BTC, ETH as margin).
notes: Tier 1 regulator action — Morgan Lewis summary of the CFTC's own staff communications. Also references CFTC Staff Letter 26-05 directly.

title: Tokenisation of Financial Assets — Final Report (FR/17/25)
key_claim: IOSCO finds tokenisation enables potential efficiency gains (shorter settlement cycles, improved collateral mobility) but adoption remains limited by interoperability challenges and lack of credible settlement assets; tokenized claims with maturity-mismatched backing increase redemption-run risk with adverse spillovers.
notes: IOSCO is the multilateral securities-regulator standards body — strictly Tier 2 (institutional). Structural anchor for the regulatory-perimeter framing; 6 months old but canonical.

title: BlackRock Set to Launch Tokenized Money-Market Funds for Investors
key_claim: BlackRock filed with the SEC to launch two new blockchain-native funds: tokenized version of BlackRock Select Treasury Based Liquidity Fund (BSTBL) and the BlackRock Daily Reinvestment Stablecoin Reserve Vehicle (BRSRV).

title: OKX Taps BlackRock's $2.5B BUIDL for Margin, Extends Custody Model with Standard Chartered
key_claim: OKX added BlackRock's BUIDL (~$2.5bn AUM) to its collateral framework with Standard Chartered as custodian — first off-exchange tokenized collateral model backed by a Tier-1 G-SIB. Yields paid out on chain.
notes: Tier 3 specialist trade press; covers same event reported across CoinDesk, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg.

title: IMF warns tokenization could bring crypto risks into global financial markets
key_claim: Per CoinDesk summary of IMF April 2026 note: distributed asset value (on-chain market value of tokenised assets ex-stablecoins) reached $27.65bn, up 4.07% in 30 days; represented asset value (underlying assets brought into tokenisation) reached $441.38bn, up 31.61% in 30 days.
notes: Tier 3 corroboration of IMF report; useful for the quantitative anchors the IMF PDF doesn't easily expose.

title: BlackRock deepens tokenization push with new onchain fund offerings
key_claim: BlackRock's BUIDL now ~$2.9bn AUM (40% of tokenized Treasury market); SEC filings cover BSTBL (tokenized version of Select Treasury Liquidity Fund) and BRSRV (Daily Reinvestment Stablecoin Reserve Vehicle for digital-asset workflows).
notes: Tier 3 corroboration of Bloomberg coverage; provides specific AUM and market share figures.

title: Franklin Templeton, Stellar Development Foundation Mark Five Years of BENJI, the First U.S.-Registered Tokenized Money Market Fund
key_claim: BENJI investors grew >140% from April 2024 to March 2026; as of 29 April 2026, BENJI suite represents $1.98bn AUM. Franklin OnChain U.S. Government Money Fund is the first U.S.-registered mutual fund to use a public blockchain as its official system of record.
notes: Tier 4 vendor source — directional. Used because it documents the BENJI growth metrics and competitive depth alongside BUIDL; AUM numbers cross-checked against rwa.xyz public tracker.
